note: The detection corpus. Real public repositories, with what Pando should work out
This exists because 'detection quality below the R-103 bar' is the top risk in
docs/plan/risk-register.md, and the mitigation is a corpus built early plus
questions-per-deploy tracked as a metric rather than a vibe. A detector that
gets better on the repo in front of you and worse everywhere else is the
`questions` is a BUDGET, not an expectation: detection may ask fewer. Asking
more fails the case, because every question is something a person has to
answer before their app runs, and R-005 says they may not know what a port is.
It counts only questions put to a PERSON. A question marked deferred is one
the trial run is expected to answer by watching the app start (R-097) — the
port questions are all of this kind. Deferred questions are printed beside
each case so that moving a question out of the budget stays visible, but they
are not charged to it: the whole point of R-097 is that nobody is asked.
Budgets are ratchets. Each one sits at what detection currently asks, so any
new question is a deliberate decision someone has to make rather than slack
quietly absorbed by a loose ceiling.

cases.name: dockerfile-at-root
cases.why: The easy case. A Dockerfile at the root leaves nothing to ask.

cases.name: node-library
cases.why: The Express library, not an app: its package.json says which files it publishes and has no start script, so there is nothing to run. Detection refuses it with that reason rather than planning a Node app that starts nothing (R-021; issue #90's bm-neg-express).

cases.name: static-site
cases.why: No server at all. Getting this wrong means building a container for a folder of HTML.

cases.name: compose-stack
cases.why: Multi-service, with a declared database and a volume. Exercises the one-primary-workload rule, and that a database the app reaches by hostname is imported as written rather than swapped for a provisioned one (R-096).

cases.name: monorepo
cases.why: Several deployable things in one repository. Pando must ask which one rather than picking, and the question has to name the candidates it found (R-105).

cases.name: dockerfile-in-subdirectory
cases.why: Compose at the root, Dockerfiles beneath it. The compose file should win — it says how the parts fit together, which the Dockerfiles do not.

cases.name: python-with-requirements
cases.why: The Python equivalent: Flask's own repository is a package under src/, refused as a library (R-021).

cases.name: go-module
cases.why: A library rather than an app: detection refuses it and says why, rather than inventing an entrypoint (R-021).

cases.name: static-with-build-step
cases.why: A build step whose output is static: index.html at the root beside a package.json that declares `vite build`. The interesting failure is detecting `static` and serving the root unbuilt, which produces a blank page rather than an error. Previously this case pointed at the whole vite repository, which is a monorepo and not this shape at all — it passed for the wrong reason.

cases.name: empty-repository
cases.why: Almost nothing to go on. Detection must return low confidence and questions rather than a confident wrong answer — R-102 is 'ask, never guess', and this is where guessing is most tempting.
